props.caption: same picture, same file
props.title: The Address Book

B01.capture_spec: C01: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white) with --tex pic=sprite, lab-shaders/01-hook-controls.gdshader. Keyframes as fractions of the beat length L (about 11.6 s): shift = 0 until 0.17 L, then 0 to 1.0 over 0.17-0.28 L, hold; zoom = 1 until 0.28 L, then 1 to 3 over 0.28-0.42 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+, no input. End state (shift 1.0, zoom 3.0): nine whole copies, aligned (probes hook-tiled-fill).
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'The Address Book' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the stage: the teal test sprite sits still, then slides left and wraps around, then shrinks into a three by three grid of copies. Label: 'same picture, same file'.
B01.motion_claim: The picture slides, then shrinks and tiles, while the label says the file never changes.

show.event: the sprite at rest, window labelled
the picture slides left and wraps
it shrinks into a three by three grid (settled by 0.42)

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a picture moving behind a window
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of 'the same picture, a different look'; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: A square with U labelled along the top (a drawn arrow pointing right) and V labelled down the left side (a drawn arrow pointing down), corner labels (0, 0) at the top left and (1, 1) at the bottom right, and a terracotta dot whose live (u, v) label updates as it moves. Caption (GLOSSARY wording): 'UV: a point's address on the shape: 0 to 1 across, 0 to 1 down'.
B02.motion_claim: The dot slides across (U grows), then down (V grows), then jumps to the top-left corner and to the bottom-right corner, its label updating each time.

show.event: square, axes, U and V labels
dot slides across: U grows
dot slides down: V grows (settled by 0.45)
dot at the top left, label (0, 0)
dot at the bottom right, label (1, 1)

B02.why: A square you can point at, with a dot whose label updates, makes 'two numbers, zero to one, V down' concrete; the real render of the same idea comes next (B04).

B03.visual_intent: Two squares side by side, one small and one large, both labelled with the same corner values (0, 0) and (1, 1) and both carrying a dot at (0.5, 0.8) with an identical label. A grey up arrow marked 'school graph' beside the small square and a terracotta down arrow marked 'V' beside the large one. Caption: 'fraction, not pixels'.
B03.motion_claim: The grey up arrow appears and is replaced by the terracotta down arrow; then the large square grows beside the small one and its dot lands on the same label.

show.event: square with the school-graph up arrow, then the V down arrow
the second, larger square, same corner labels
both dots at (0.5, 0.8), same label
caption: fraction, not pixels

B03.why: Two squares of different size carrying identical corner labels show 'a fraction, not a pixel count' at a glance; a table would only list it.

B04.capture_spec: C02: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white), lab-shaders/02-address-map.gdshader, still PNG 3840x2160 (16:9 window, the square quad centered at 0.45 of the width). Corner colours (probes): top left (0.02, 0.02, 0.50), top right (0.98, 0.02, 0.50), bottom left (0.02, 0.98, 0.50), bottom right (0.98, 0.98, 0.50).
B04.visual_intent: Code card at left with the one-line address-map shader; at right a real Godot window with a centered square showing the red-green picture (red grows to the right, green grows downward, blue held at half), corner labels outside the square landing in turn: (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1).
B04.motion_claim: The corner labels land with the words: red grows to the right (top right), green grows downward (bottom left).

show.event: COLOR line highlighted; the address picture on screen
(0, 0) and (1, 0): red grows to the right
(0, 1) and (1, 1): green grows downward
blue held at half

B04.runner_up: manim: a UV square drawn with a colour gradient
B04.why: The address map is Godot's own picture of UV (the Godot tutorial's first UV example); the render is the evidence, the Manim square already carried the numbers.

B05.visual_intent: Left, a small grid of outline pixel cells labelled 'the shape' with one cell ringed in terracotta and tagged with its address (0.7, 0.5); right, the picture (a cream card with the teal test sprite) labelled 'TEXTURE: the node's own picture' (GLOSSARY wording). An arrow runs from the ringed pixel to the same relative spot on the picture, where a terracotta dot lands; a teal swatch travels back along the arrow and the ringed pixel fills with teal. Small tag on the arrow: 'texture()'.
B05.motion_claim: An arrow goes out from the pixel to a spot on the picture, and the color found there travels back and fills the pixel.

show.event: pixel ringed, address tag
arrow reaches the picture; dot lands
teal swatch returns along the arrow
the pixel is filled teal

B05.why: A lookup is a question going out and a colour coming back; a drawn arrow and a returning swatch say exactly that, with the pixel and the picture both visible.

cues.label: COLOR: the color of the pixel being drawn

props.caption: fragment(): runs once for each pixel the shape covers; sets its color

B06.capture_spec: C03: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite). No material until 0.58 L, then --material-at assigns lab-shaders/03-lookup.gdshader; the picture must not change. Render L + 1 s (L about 11.6 s), 30 fps, Forward+. Verified: with the shader and without it, 0 of 230,400 pixels differ, largest channel difference 0.0 (verify-identity.gd D1). Probes (fill-window): middle (0.372, 0.639, 0.569) teal, eyes (0.980, 0.977, 0.961) at (0.4, 0.44) and (0.6, 0.44), corner (0.851, 0.835, 0.792) = stage.
B06.visual_intent: Code card at left with the three-line lookup shader; at right a real Godot window showing the test sprite drawn plainly, with no shader. At 'Nothing is changed' the lookup shader is switched on and the picture does not change at all. A caption defines fragment (GLOSSARY wording): 'fragment(): runs once for each pixel the shape covers; sets its color'. Readout 'shader on' at the switch; then a terracotta ring settles on the sprite's square with the readout 'unchanged'.
B06.motion_claim: The shader switches on and nothing changes: the picture is pixel for pixel the same.

show.event: function line: runs once for every pixel the shape covers
COLOR line: TEXTURE is the node's own picture; read it at the pixel's own address
the lookup shader switches on (readout 'shader on'); COLOR defined
ring on the picture: unchanged

B06.why: The line and its unchanged result side by side is the claim, and watching the shader switch on with no change is the proof; a code trace alone would not show 'comes out as it went in'.

B07.visual_intent: Left, a large cream card labelled 'the picture' holding the teal test sprite and a small terracotta tick at its top-left corner; over it a terracotta-outlined rectangle labelled 'the shape'. Right, a framed panel labelled 'what you see' showing the part of the picture inside the outline. Caption: 'address moves it'.
B07.motion_claim: The outlined window slides right across the fixed picture while the panel's contents shift left, then it slides back.

show.event: picture card, window outline, panel
window slides right; panel content shifts left
window slides back; caption lands

B07.runner_up: ShaderLab: a real render with the quad ringed
B07.why: 'The shape is a window' is an analogy; only a drawing can slide a window over a fixed picture and show the contents change.

props.title: Copy, bend, look up
props.note: UV is read-only in fragment() · Godot 4.7 documentation, checked in Godot 4.7.2

B08.visual_intent: A cream code card with the real seven-line template; focus lands on the function, then the copy line, then the empty bend line, then the lookup line as each is named.
B08.motion_claim: Line focus steps through copy, bend, look up on the words.

show.event: fragment: the address is read-only
copy the address
bend the copy
look up with the copy

B08.why: Paced line focus lands on 'copy', 'bend', 'look up' as each is spoken; the pattern is real, compiled code.
